nodes.name: Rain
nodes.desc: Wet Pacific air dumps heavy precipitation on the mountain, feeding the old-growth forest on its lower slopes.

nodes.name: Snowpack & glaciers
nodes.desc: Deep winter snow buries the high meadows and sets how early plants can grow. Its melt feeds the streams.

nodes.name: Short summer sun
nodes.desc: Meadow plants have only a brief snow-free season, so they flower and set seed quickly once the snow melts.

nodes.name: Volcanic mountain soil
nodes.desc: Thin, young soils built on volcanic rock and glacial debris support the forests and meadows.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down fallen logs, needles and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Western hemlock
nodes.desc: A shade-tolerant conifer of the lower, wetter forests where the old-growth stands are found.

nodes.name: Subalpine fir
nodes.desc: Grows at and just below the tree line. Its seeds feed birds and squirrels, and its clumps trap snow and help form meadows.

nodes.name: Avalanche lily
nodes.desc: A meadow wildflower that blooms right after the snow melts, one of the most recorded plants near the park.

nodes.name: Fireweed
nodes.desc: A tall wildflower of clearings and meadows. Deer, pikas and bumble bees feed on it, according to records and Wikipedia.

nodes.name: Thinleaf huckleberry
nodes.desc: A berry shrub of subalpine slopes. Its berries are eaten by bears and many other animals.

nodes.name: Hoary marmot
nodes.desc: A big ground squirrel of rocky alpine meadows. Wikipedia says it eats leaves, flowers, grasses and sedges.

nodes.name: American pika
nodes.desc: A small relative of rabbits living in rock slides. Eats grasses, sedges and fireweed, and stacks hay piles for winter.

nodes.name: Mountain goat
nodes.desc: Grazes grasses, herbs, sedges and low shrubs on steep slopes. Cougars are its main predator, and cliffs are its best defence.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: Browses shrubs and herbs, including fireweed. A staple prey of cougars.

nodes.name: Elk
nodes.desc: A large grazer and browser of forest and meadow. Recorded in GBIF data under the name red deer.

nodes.name: Douglas squirrel
nodes.desc: Eats mostly conifer seeds and stores cones in a midden. Also eats fungi and berries.

nodes.name: Gapper's red-backed vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent of the forest floor, eaten by foxes, hawks and bears in GloBI records.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats berries, plants, small mammals and deer or elk. Often takes over carcasses left by cougars.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Hunts voles, mice and small mammals and eats carrion. GloBI also lists deer and birds among its food.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A hawk that hunts small mammals such as voles and also snakes and birds.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever scavenger that feeds on carcasses along with small prey and scraps.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: The mountain lion hunts mainly deer and elk, and also goats. Bears often take over its kills.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: An eagle of open alpine ground that preys on marmots, pikas and other mammals.
